subject: social-studies
unit_title: Foundations of World Historical and Geographical Inquiry
title: Launch and diagnostic: framing questions and historical significance
essential_question: How do world historians and geographers make sense of a global past?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about framing questions and historical significance, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use primary and secondary evidence, maps, or data to communicate understanding of framing questions and historical significance.
Check, revise, or improve work about framing questions and historical significance using stated success criteria and source reliability.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about framing questions and historical significance.
The learner gives cited evidence and reasoning rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner distinguishes primary from secondary evidence and notes each source's perspective.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil or accessible response tool
unit source set retrieved from a named public repository
map, atlas, or data display appropriate to the unit

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “framing questions and historical significance.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Examine maps, data, and primary and secondary sources; establish provenance; contextualize competing perspectives; and support a historical, geographic, economic, or civic claim with cited evidence. Keep the explanation centered on framing questions and historical significance. Name the success criteria and model how to check a claim against its sources.

Complete two supported source-based or analytical tasks about framing questions and historical significance. After each step ask: “What evidence supports that move, and how do we know the source is reliable?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of framing questions and historical significance and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.

In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about framing questions and historical significance; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of framing questions and historical significance and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about framing questions and historical significance; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, use and citation of evidence, fair representation of perspectives, and revision. Accept multiple valid interpretations when they meet the criteria and are supported by the sources. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

source_use.primary_secondary: Identify each source as primary or secondary, state who produced it and when, and note what perspective it represents and what it omits.
anchor_sources: Historical map collections (Library of Congress Geography and Map Division)
United Nations statistical series (United Nations Digital Library)
source_use.retrieval_note: Retrieve the actual text, map, or data from the named repository. This package names sources and never reproduces or paraphrases their wording as though quoted.

citation_requirement: Every claim offered as evidence names its source with enough detail for another reader to locate it. Quotations must be transcribed by the learner from the retrieved source; this package supplies no quoted text.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for framing questions and historical significance, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the reasoning for framing questions and historical significance works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of framing questions and historical significance, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Ask which source supports the claim and how it was corroborated. Do not supply the claim, the wording, or the citation.
Decline to draft or revise graded argumentative prose. Offer evidence analysis, questions, structure options, or feedback on the learner's own draft instead.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking framing questions and historical significance mastered.

tutor_boundary: The tutor may help locate, read, contextualize, and analyze evidence, and may question the learner's reasoning. The tutor may not draft, rewrite, or supply the wording of a graded argument, thesis, or citation. A static, tutor-free path through this lesson is always available.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use source analysis, map or data work, discussion, an evidence-based claim with citation, and an inquiry product; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two separate occasions.
extension: Apply framing questions and historical significance under a new constraint, compare two interpretations or regional perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, recorded, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media and maps.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Handle war, genocide, enslavement, oppression, displacement, identity, and belief with accurate context, documented evidence, and human dignity.
Do not require a learner to represent an identity or to argue for an injustice in simulation.
Represent contested issues with more than one well-sourced perspective rather than a single settled answer.

media.suggestion: Optional map, data display, timeline, document image, or short clip supporting framing questions and historical significance.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or printed model, or facilitator description.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of framing questions and historical significance in public life or local records. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

Complete two supported source-based or analytical tasks about maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns. After each step ask: “What evidence supports that move, and how do we know the source is reliable?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.

formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, use and citation of evidence, fair representation of perspectives, and revision. source_use.primary_secondary: Identify each source as primary or secondary, state who produced it and when, and note what perspective it represents and what it omits.

source_use.retrieval_note: Retrieve the actual text, map, or data from the named repository. This package names sources and never reproduces or paraphrases their wording as though quoted.

citation_requirement: Every claim offered as evidence names its source with enough detail for another reader to locate it. Quotations must be transcribed by the learner from the retrieved source; this package supplies no quoted text.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the reasoning for maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Ask which source supports the claim and how it was corroborated. Do not supply the claim, the wording, or the citation.
Decline to draft or revise graded argumentative prose. Offer evidence analysis, questions, structure options, or feedback on the learner's own draft instead.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use source analysis, map or data work, discussion, an evidence-based claim with citation, and an inquiry product; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two separate occasions.
extension: Apply maps, graphs, and large-scale patterns under a new constraint, compare two interpretations or regional perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, recorded, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media and maps.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.

learning_objectives: Practice connecting historical patterns to present issues with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use primary and secondary evidence, maps, or data to communicate understanding of connecting historical patterns to present issues.
Check, revise, or improve work about connecting historical patterns to present issues using stated success criteria and source reliability.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about connecting historical patterns to present issues.
The learner gives cited evidence and reasoning rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner distinguishes primary from secondary evidence and notes each source's perspective.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil or accessible response tool
unit source set retrieved from a named public repository
map, atlas, or data display appropriate to the unit

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “connecting historical patterns to present issues.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Examine maps, data, and primary and secondary sources; establish provenance; contextualize competing perspectives; and support a historical, geographic, economic, or civic claim with cited evidence. Keep the explanation centered on connecting historical patterns to present issues. Name the success criteria and model how to check a claim against its sources.

Complete two supported source-based or analytical tasks about connecting historical patterns to present issues. After each step ask: “What evidence supports that move, and how do we know the source is reliable?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of connecting historical patterns to present issues and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.

In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about connecting historical patterns to present issues; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of connecting historical patterns to present issues and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about connecting historical patterns to present issues; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, use and citation of evidence, fair representation of perspectives, and revision. Accept multiple valid interpretations when they meet the criteria and are supported by the sources. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

source_use.primary_secondary: Identify each source as primary or secondary, state who produced it and when, and note what perspective it represents and what it omits.
anchor_sources: United Nations population and development statistical series (United Nations Digital Library)
Paris Agreement, 2015 (United Nations Digital Library)
source_use.retrieval_note: Retrieve the actual text, map, or data from the named repository. This package names sources and never reproduces or paraphrases their wording as though quoted.

citation_requirement: Every claim offered as evidence names its source with enough detail for another reader to locate it. Quotations must be transcribed by the learner from the retrieved source; this package supplies no quoted text.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for connecting historical patterns to present issues, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the reasoning for connecting historical patterns to present issues works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of connecting historical patterns to present issues, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Ask which source supports the claim and how it was corroborated. Do not supply the claim, the wording, or the citation.
Decline to draft or revise graded argumentative prose. Offer evidence analysis, questions, structure options, or feedback on the learner's own draft instead.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking connecting historical patterns to present issues mastered.

tutor_boundary: The tutor may help locate, read, contextualize, and analyze evidence, and may question the learner's reasoning. The tutor may not draft, rewrite, or supply the wording of a graded argument, thesis, or citation. A static, tutor-free path through this lesson is always available.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use source analysis, map or data work, discussion, an evidence-based claim with citation, and an inquiry product; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two separate occasions.
extension: Apply connecting historical patterns to present issues under a new constraint, compare two interpretations or regional perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, recorded, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media and maps.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Handle war, genocide, enslavement, oppression, displacement, identity, and belief with accurate context, documented evidence, and human dignity.
Do not require a learner to represent an identity or to argue for an injustice in simulation.
Represent contested issues with more than one well-sourced perspective rather than a single settled answer.

media.suggestion: Optional map, data display, timeline, document image, or short clip supporting connecting historical patterns to present issues.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or printed model, or facilitator description.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of connecting historical patterns to present issues in public life or local records. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
